A marathon plan usually runs sixteen to twenty weeks and builds weekly mileage slowly, no more than about ten percent a week. Most running should be easy, at a pace where you can hold a conversation. One long run each weekend grows from ten to thirty two kilometres, followed by a cutback week every third or fourth week. A single quality session, tempo or intervals, improves speed. The last three weeks are a taper with reduced volume so the legs arrive fresh. Fuelling matters, see [[Race day nutrition]].
